problem: Embodied navigation benchmarks (ObjectNav, OVON, PIN) score success at arrival near the goal, so an agent can reach a wrong instance (e.g. white striped vs white floral mug) and still count as a hit. Verification is at best a prompt-level step inside navigation (CompassNav, IEVE) and is not evaluated as a standalone decision problem.
motivation: Deployment needs to confirm the correct instance before interaction, and fine-grained attributes are often invisible at navigation distance or lie on non-frontal surfaces, so multi-view close inspection is needed. A controlled offline testbed that removes locomotion allows ablating detection, query mode and view selection.
key_idea: Define Active Instance Verification as a finite-horizon decision process over a 6-sector offline multi-view graph with trap views and unreachable sectors, and release PInVerify (3,000 balanced episodes) with training-free and LoRA-trained MLLM reference agents.
insight: Detection quality and calibration matter more than view selection: GT boxes raise SV-Attr from 0.844 to 0.875 (Pos 0.652 to 0.758), and Random, Angular FPS and LLM-NBV land within 0.2pp (0.848-0.850), i.e. no reliable gain from active viewpoint choice. The best query mode depends on model calibration: attribute decomposition helps Qwen3-VL-4B but hurts the rejection-biased Qwen3-VL-8B (0.797) and the over-confirming SenseNova-SI (neg_same 0.526). SFT fixes the strong 'no match' bias of the base model (Pos 0.146 to 0.759) but induces confirmation bias (neg_same 0.814).
method: Task formulation: episode (descriptions Q, query object, target object, sector graph G); actions NAV to one of K=6 sectors or YES/NO; horizon T=6; metrics accuracy per pair type and Average Steps to Decision (ASD), plus navigation failure rate.

Offline capture pipeline: HM3D/PInNED scenes, 12-sector azimuth discretization with 6 active sectors at 60° spacing, far (1.4-1.7 m) and near (0.9-1.2 m) rings, RGB+mask+GT box per capture, per-category mask thresholds to mark trap views, unreachable sectors when no navigable point is within ±30°.

Pair construction: for each target, one positive, one neg_same (same-category distractor description) and one neg_diff (cross-category) pair; 3,000 eval pairs balanced 1:1:1 across 71 instances and 35 scenes.

Training-free pipeline: MLLM attribute decomposition (up to 8 attributes with quoted evidence), Grounding DINO crop, per-attribute Yes/No/Unsure verification, visibility-weighted tracker (low-confidence views down-weighted 0.2x), attribute-majority fusion with adaptive stopping.
NBV strategies: Random, LLM-based direction selection, and Angular Farthest-Point Sampling maximizing minimum arc distance to visited azimuths.

Trained end-to-end agent: Qwen3-VL-4B with LoRA (rank 16) taking scene RGB plus object crop, output <think>/<answer> with verification and next action; SFT on ~22K templated CoT samples, then DPO, GRPO (G=4) or GSPO with reward 0.5 verify + 0.4 action + 0.1 format.
Embedding baselines: CLIP and SigLIP2 image-text matching, single-view and multi-view, with merged descriptions.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-4B (LoRA SFT+GSPO for trained agent; frozen for training-free), Qwen3-VL-8B, SenseNova-SI-1.2-InternVL3-8B, CLIP, SigLIP2, Grounding DINO detector
setting.training_data: Trained agent: ~22K SFT samples and an RL pool from a disjoint PInVerify training pool (15,225 pairs, 145 HM3D scenes, 264 instances), labels templated from benchmark ground truth; training-free variants use none
setting.observation: Monocular RGB (360x640) per sector view plus detector crop of the candidate object; 3 natural-language descriptions
setting.action_space: Discrete: NAV to one of 6 relative sectors on an offline graph, or terminal YES/NO
setting.simulator: Offline pre-captured multi-view images from Habitat/HM3D (PInNED objects); no online simulator at evaluation
setting.privileged: Default uses Grounding DINO; GT-box ablation uses ground-truth bounding boxes; trained agent labels and rewards use benchmark GT visibility metadata (training only)

numbers.extra: Grounding DINO detection, adaptive stopping T=6
Grounding DINO crops at inference; ~22K SFT samples plus RL pool

numbers_note: Results are on PInVerify's own 3,000-episode test set (no official split names; 'test' used). Metrics printed as fractions were converted to percent. Cross-model rows: SenseNova-SI MV-Direct+Rnd 0.833, Qwen3-VL-8B 0.797, SigLIP2 0.801, CLIP 0.771.
results: The best training-free MLLM baseline (Qwen3-VL-4B, MV-Attr+LLM) reaches 85.0% overall, 4.9pp above the best embedding baseline (SigLIP2, 80.1%). SFT+GSPO reaches 85.6% (88.9% with GT boxes) with much lower NavFail (9% vs 28%) and ASD (1.62 vs 2.34), trading neg_same accuracy for positive confirmation. The three NBV strategies are indistinguishable within the ±1.3pp CI.
limitations: Reuses PInNED scenes, objects and English descriptions (indoor HM3D, Objaverse-XL objects), and is offline, so live-control challenges are untested
Single seed with no multi-seed runs; many differences are within the ±1.3pp CI, and only open-source ≤8B MLLMs are evaluated
Trained-agent labels and rewards depend on benchmark ground truth, and the agent shows confirmation bias (neg_same drops to about 0.84)
